risks: No contact with patients; the risk is misuse of results, for example ranking bed managers or units, which is avoided by reporting at hospital level.
consent: Individual consent is not sought for this service evaluation of existing logs under the data governance approval; patients are informed through the hospital's notice on the use of operational data.
data: Linked data on the hospital analytics server, with record numbers replaced by study codes before analysis; no data leave the hospital.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients admitted at night, older patients and those admitted to services with lower sensitivity may be systematically missed by the flag. Accuracy is reported by time of day and admitting service, and by age group, so that the command centre can see whom the flag fails.
effectiveness: The evaluation is useful whether the flag performs well or badly; a poor result redirects escalation effort.
efficiency: Existing logs and about 25 analyst days.
grants: None needed for the evaluation; a later recalibration or new model could seek funding.
partnerships: Command centre staff, emergency and inpatient physicians, bed managers, and a patient partner from the hospital's patient and family advisory council.
rebPath: Service evaluation of operational data under data governance approval DG-2026-311; before publication the hospital research ethics board will be asked whether review is required, following the TCPS 2 guidance on program evaluation.
limitations: One hospital; escalation may bias accuracy downward; the reference standard depends on timestamps.
summary: Evaluation of existing logs under data governance approval, with equity reporting by time of day, service and age.
